children: India’s automobile exports rose 22.2 per cent year-on-year to 6,81,338 units in August 2026, compared with 5,57,446 units in the same month last year, according to data released by the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM).
Two-wheelers led the growth with 28.5 per cent growth.

Passenger-vehicle exports were more subdued, declining 17 per cent to 68,230 units from 82,246 units in August 2025. In the segment, passenger car exports declined by 51.5 per cent in August over the same period last year. The geopolitical disruptions led to the decline, say industry sources. However, PV data does not include data for BMW, Mercedes, JLR, Tata Motors and Volvo Auto, SIAM notes.

Two-wheelers accounted for the bulk of the increase, with exports rising 28.5 per cent to 5,55,292 units from 4,32,033 units a year earlier. Motorcycles were the largest contributor within the segment, with exports increasing 33.4 per cent to 4,86,325 units from 3,64,487 units. Scooter exports rose 5.1 per cent to 68,085 units.
The decline in PV exports was witnessed among all the OEMs and in all segments - mini, compact and mid-size, says the data.
Kotak Institutional Equities’ report on Automobiles & Components said that exports saw weak trends across OEMs owing to logistical disruptions arising from the Middle East crisis.

Commenting on the exports data, Poonam Upadhyay, Director, Crisil Ratings said that the trend suggests Indian automotive manufacturing is moving up the value chain rather than simply benefiting from a cyclical demand upswing. “Global markets are increasingly viewing India as a sourcing hub for compact SUVs, not just entry-level cars. Whether this marks a durable structural shift will depend on how quickly OEMs expand SUV-focused capacity and platforms to meet what appears to be sustained international demand,” she added.
She drew attention to utility vehicle exports, which she noted, rose ~23 per cent to around 2.03 lakh units during April-August FY27.

“This is far more than a one-off spike. In FY26, UV exports had already reached 4.45 lakh units, virtually matching passenger car exports of 4.49 lakh units. That gap has effectively disappeared this fiscal year. What was a niche export segment a few years ago has now overtaken India’s traditional hatchback-led export story,” she added.

title: Auto exports rise 22% in August led by two-wheelers
